# gi.validate.check_foreign_key { #bedrock_ge.gi.validate.check_foreign_key }

```python
gi.validate.check_foreign_key(foreign_key, parent_table, table_with_foreign_key)
```

Validates referential integrity between two tables by checking foreign key relationships.

This function ensures that all foreign key values in a child table exist in the corresponding
parent table, maintaining data integrity in the GIS database.

## Example {.doc-section .doc-section-example}

```python
check_foreign_key("project_uid", projects_df, locations_df)
```

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name                   | Type                             | Description                                            | Default    |
|------------------------|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| foreign_key            | str                              | The name of the column that serves as the foreign key. | _required_ |
| parent_table           | pd.DataFrame \| gpd.GeoDataFrame | The parent table containing the primary keys.          | _required_ |
| table_with_foreign_key | pd.DataFrame \| gpd.GeoDataFrame | The child table containing the foreign keys.           | _required_ |

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type   | Description                                         |
|--------|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|
|        | bool   | True if all foreign keys exist in the parent table. |

## Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type       | Description                                                                    |
|--------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | ValueError | If any foreign key values in the child table do not exist in the parent table. |
